items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: I mean you talk to Sweets Edison about Buddy and he says, “Oh man,” he gets like rekindled.

ctx.x: Well it’s good to hear — I mean you phrase it in a positive sense, that he was a—

Well the people that put him down are the people that were mediocre and that couldn’t play. And they hated him. I think it’s very simple. I mean you talk to Sweets Edison about Buddy and he says, “Oh man,” he gets like rekindled. You’d get ready to play, and Buddy’d be there and he’d be propelling you along, making it easier for you to play.
He had upstate people too. Joe Romano, Pat LaBarbera, Sal—
